text: Hello, this is the fraud prevention team at your bank. We have detected a suspicious transaction of forty-nine thousand rupees on your card at an online store. Did you make this purchase?
tell: A fake fraud alert makes you anxious and cooperative; it is the setup for asking you to 'cancel' with a code.

text: Congratulations, your credit card has earned reward points worth eight thousand rupees that expire today. I can redeem them straight into your account while we are on the call.
tell: Unsolicited reward redemption over the phone is a lure; points are redeemed only inside the bank's own app or site.

text: Hi, I'm calling from your bank's security department about a new payee that was just added to your online banking. If this wasn't you, I can block it for you immediately.
tell: Offering to 'block' a threat you cannot see gives the caller a reason to request authentication codes.

text: For your security I'll confirm some details first. Your card ends in four three one seven and your date of birth is on file. I'm a senior fraud analyst and this line is recorded.
tell: Reciting partial card data and 'recorded line' to sound official; this data is commonly bought from breaches.

text: I am calling from the refunds division. The amount wrongly debited from your account has already been approved for reversal, it only needs your confirmation on this call.
tell: Refunds never require you to approve anything or share a code; a 'confirmation' step is how money leaves.

text: I work in the bank's anti-fraud unit together with the police. We are tracing a criminal who has cloned your card, and we need your help to catch him in the act.
tell: Recruiting you as a helper in a police sting flatters and disarms; real police never need your codes or money.

text: Please don't open your banking app while we fix this. The fraudster is monitoring your logins and will move faster if they see any activity on the account.
tell: Keeps you from seeing the transactions the caller is initiating in real time.

text: Do not call the number on the back of your card right now. Those lines are compromised and the criminals could intercept your call.
tell: The number on your card is the safe channel; any caller discouraging it is the criminal.

text: Stay on the line with me, and if any branch staff contact you in the next hour, do not discuss this case with them, because they may be involved.
tell: Casting real bank staff as suspects pre-empts the intervention that would stop the fraud.

text: The fraudulent payment is still pending and will be processed in ten minutes. After that I can no longer stop it, and the money will be gone for good.
tell: Countdown on a transaction you cannot see pushes you to hand over the code before thinking.

text: Your reward points lapse at midnight and after that they cannot be restored. Let us finish this quickly before the offer closes.
tell: Loss-aversion deadline on a benefit, to rush past the fact that redemption never needs a code read aloud.

text: Another attempt to withdraw funds has just started. We have to secure your account within the next few minutes or the attackers will empty it completely.
tell: Escalating live 'attacks' keep the victim reactive and compliant.

text: You will receive a one time password now to cancel the transaction. Please read the code to me the moment it arrives, and do not share it with anyone else.
tell: The OTP authorises the fraudster's transaction; 'don't share it with anyone else' while asking for it is a contradiction.

text: To receive the refund, open your UPI app and approve the collect request I have sent, then enter your PIN to accept the money.
tell: A collect request with a PIN pays the requester; you never enter a PIN to receive money.

text: To protect your savings I'll move them into a safe account set up in your name. Read me the authentication code your bank sends so we can create the new payee.
tell: Banks never ask you to move money to a 'safe account'; the new payee belongs to the fraudster.
